name: Media Law & Right to Information
exam: AKNU Media Law including Right to Information exam
new_code: name of the Act it belongs to (Constitution, IPC with its BNS 2023 equivalent, Cinematograph Act 1952, Cable TV Act 1995, RTI Act 2005, IT Act 2000)
example: Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act 2005, or Section 499 IPC now Section 356 BNS
example_te: Section 8(1)(j) — RTI Act lo; Section 499 IPC ippudu BNS Section 356
terms: 'freedom of the press', 'reasonable restriction', 'pre-censorship', 'defamation', 'obscenity', 'sedition', 'contempt', 'certification', 'Programme Code', 'public authority', 'PIO', 'exemption', 'information commission', 'intermediary', 'blocking', 'safe harbour'

episodes.s: Bennett Coleman — what mass media are, who owns the press, films, radio and television, and why visual media are treated differently
episodes.cover: Types of mass media and their arrival in India; ownership of the press (families, companies, trusts; Press Commissions on concentration; foreign cap), films (private), radio and television (Government monopoly under Sec 4 Telegraph Act to Prasar Bharati and private satellite/FM/DTH); visual vs non-visual media and impact on minds (Abbas, Rangarajan, Ramesh); Bennett Coleman's direct-effect test; CAB on airwaves; the regulator table

episodes.s: Sakal Papers — Art 19(1)(a) and the freedom of the press, Art 19(2), the four newspaper cases, price-page, newsprint, pre-censorship and advertising
episodes.cover: Ambedkar's view; the seven components of press freedom (Romesh Thappar, Brij Bhushan, Bennett Coleman, Indian Express); Art 19(2)'s eight grounds, proximate nexus (Lohia), the First Amendment; Express Newspapers 1958, Sakal 1962, Bennett Coleman 1972, Indian Express 1985; Price and Page Act and Order; Newsprint Control Order and policy; no licensing, Brij Bhushan, Sahara postponement; Hamdard Dawakhana vs Tata Press on commercial speech; Common Cause on Government ads

episodes.s: Rajagopal — defamation, obscenity, blasphemy, sedition, hate speech and contempt as restrictions on the press
episodes.cover: Civil defamation elements and defences; Sec 499-502 IPC/BNS 356 with four Explanations and ten Exceptions, Sec 199 CrPC, K.M. Mathew editor presumption, Subramanian Swamy; Rajagopal's privacy, public-official and no-prior-restraint rules; obscenity Sec 292/BNS 294, Ranjit Udeshi (Hicklin), Samaresh Bose, Aveek Sarkar (community standards), Sec 67 IT Act, Indecent Representation Act; Sec 295A/BNS 299 and Ramji Lal Modi, Secs 95-96 CrPC forfeiture; sedition Sec 124A, Kedar Nath, Vombatkere 2022, BNS Sec 152, Sec 153A and Amish Devgan; Contempt of Courts Act Secs 2, 3-7, 13, Namboodiripad, Duda, Prashant Bhushan, Sahara v SEBI

episodes.s: Tata Press — the Working Journalists Act, advertising revenue and Government ads, press monopolies and the MRTP Act, registration and the Press Council
episodes.cover: WJ Act 1955 Secs 2(f), 3-7, 9-13, 17 and the Wage Boards (Express Newspapers 1958 to Majithia and ABP 2014), the Labour Codes; advertising as the press's economic base, DAVP/CBC, Common Cause guidelines, Ushodaya ad boycott, regulation of ad content, paid news; MRTP Act 1969 and the press, Press Commissions, Competition Act 2002; PRB Act 1867 to the Press and Registration of Periodicals Act 2023; Press Council Act 1978 Secs 4, 13, 14, 15 and the norms; NBDSA and BCCC

episodes.s: K.A. Abbas — films and free speech, why pre-censorship is valid for films, the Cinematograph Act and the film cases
episodes.cover: Films within Art 19(1)(a); Abbas's five reasons and two conditions; Cinematograph Act Secs 2-9 (CBFC, U/UA 7+/13+/16+/A/S, Sec 4A TV version, Sec 5B and the 1991 Guidelines, Sec 6 revision and Shankarappa, Secs 6AA-6AB piracy, FCAT abolition 2021), Part III and State Cinemas Acts under Entry 33/60; Raj Kapoor, Rangarajan (spark in a powder keg), Bobby Art (Bandit Queen), Ramesh (Tamas), Anand Patwardhan, Prakash Jha, Viacom 18 (Padmaavat), Indibily; judicial review of certification; OTT self-classification

episodes.s: Cricket Association of Bengal — the Government monopoly in broadcasting, the Chanda and Verghese Committees, Prasar Bharati, and the freedom to telecast
episodes.cover: History of AIR and DD; Sec 4 Telegraph Act and Entry 31; reasons for and objections to a Government department; Chanda Committee 1966, Verghese Committee 1978 (Akash Bharati), Joshi Committee; Prasar Bharati Act 1990 Secs 3, 4, 12, 13, 14, 23, 32 and the autonomy debate; effect of television and the five phases of policy; commercial advertising and the Commercial Code; internal scrutiny (Broadcasting Code) and judicial review — Ramesh, Odyssey, LIC v Manubhai Shah, Anand Patwardhan, CAB, Sports Signals Act and BCCI 2017; Cable Act Secs 3-20 with the Programme and Advertising Codes, uplinking guidelines, FM phases, community radio, DTH, TRAI, Telecommunications Act 2023

episodes.s: Ramesh v Union of India — constitutional restrictions on broadcasting, Art 246 and the Seventh Schedule, taxation and licensing of the media
episodes.cover: Broadcast as publication — defamation, obscenity, religious offences, contempt; the Programme Code as Art 19(2) expanded and its doubtful clauses; enforcement (IMC, Sec 19-20 Cable Act, NBDSA); Art 246 with List I Entries 31, 60, 92, 97, List II Entries 1, 33, 55, 62, List III Entries 1, 2, 14, 39; CAB, Purvi Communication (aspect theory), Viacom 18; taxes on the press (Indian Express, Printers Mysore), entertainment tax and GST after the 101st Amendment; licences and fees — Telegraph/Telecommunications Act authorisation, uplinking, FM, community radio, cable, DTH, cinema halls, CBFC; AGR case on licence fee vs tax; the entry table

episodes.s: The MKSS movement — the development of the right to information in India from Raj Narain to the RTI Act 2005
episodes.cover: Right to know in Art 19(1)(a) and 21 — Raj Narain, S.P. Gupta, Reliance Petrochemicals, CAB, Dinesh Trivedi, ADR and PUCL; the secrecy laws — Official Secrets Act Secs 3, 5 (Iftikhar Gilani, Rafale), Sec 123 Evidence Act, Conduct Rules Rule 11; the MKSS jan sunwais and Beawar; NCPRI and the Press Council draft; State Acts (Tamil Nadu, Goa, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Delhi, Maharashtra); FOI Act 2002; NAC draft and RTI Act 2005 (15 June, 12 October); international developments (Sweden 1766, US FOIA, UK 2000, ICCPR Art 19, Tromso); the timeline

episodes.s: CBSE v Aditya Bandopadhyay — the Right to Information Act 2005 section by section and its implementation
episodes.cover: Preamble; Sec 2(f), (h), (i), (j), (n); Sec 3 citizens; Sec 4 proactive disclosure; Sec 5 PIOs and APIOs; Sec 6 request, no reasons, transfer; Sec 7 thirty days, 48 hours, fees, free if late; Sec 8(1)(a)-(j) with 8(2) override and 8(3) twenty years, DPDP Sec 44(3) amendment; Secs 9-11; Secs 12-17 Commissions and the 2019 amendment, Namit Sharma, Anjali Bhardwaj; Sec 18 complaints (Manipur), Sec 19 appeals and burden, Sec 20 penalties; Secs 21-31 incl. Sec 22 override, 23 bar, 24 exempt organisations and proviso; RTI Rules 2012; achievements and problems of implementation

episodes.s: Subhash Chandra Agarwal — the RTI decisions of the Supreme Court, the Central Information Commission and the State Commissions
episodes.cover: Subhash Chandra Agarwal 2019 (CJI's office, fiduciary, personal information balancing); Girish Deshpande; Thalappalam and D.A.V. College; Jayantilal Mistry (RBI) and the pending review; Bihar PSC; Khanapuram Gandaiah; Kerala PSC; UPSC v Angesh Kumar; Yashwant Sinha (OSA); CIC v High Court of Gujarat; CIC decisions — file notings, political parties 2013, PMO, President and Governors, BCCI, Attorney General, ministers' assets, demonetisation minutes, collegium (Anjali Bhardwaj 2022); A.P. and Telangana SICs; the judiciary as public authority

episodes.s: R.K. Anand — sting operations, trial by media, privacy, paid news, self-regulation and the law of advertising
episodes.cover: Stings — Tehelka, cash for questions, Aniruddha Bahal, Sec 65B evidence, Uma Khurana guidelines, NBDSA rules; trial by media — Zahira, Law Commission 200th Report, Sahara postponement, M.P. Lohia, Manu Sharma, Nilesh Navlakha, Arnab Goswami, MHA media briefing advisories; privacy — Rajagopal, Puttaswamy, Nipun Saxena, JJ Act 74, POCSO 23, Mr X v Hospital Z, right to be forgotten, DPDP journalistic exemption; paid news — Press Council report, Ashok Chavan, EC committees; self-regulation — Press Council, NBDSA, BCCC, ASCI; advertising law — CPA 2019 Secs 2(28), 21, 89, CCPA guidelines, Patanjali case, DMR Act, COTPA Sec 5, PCPNDT Sec 22, Emblems Act, Cable Advertising Code, FSSA, RPA Secs 126-127A, Gemini TV, comparative advertising; reporting restrictions and protection of sources (Pegasus, NewsClick guidelines)

episodes.t: Two Girls and a Facebook Post
episodes.s: Shreya Singhal and Anuradha Bhasin — the IT Act, the IT Rules 2021, internet shutdowns, the DPDP Act and the regulation of digital media
episodes.cover: IT Act Secs 2(1)(w), 66A, 66E, 67-67B, 69, 69A and the 2009 Blocking Rules, 79; Shreya Singhal's three holdings and the PUCL follow-up; IT Rules 2021 — Rule 3 due diligence and takedown, Rule 4 SSMIs and traceability, Rule 3A GACs, Part III Code of Ethics and the three-tier mechanism for digital news and OTT, Rule 16 emergency blocking, the Bombay HC stay (AGIJ), Kunal Kamra on the fact-check unit; Anuradha Bhasin and the 2017/2024 suspension rules, Faheema Shirin, Telecommunications Act Sec 20; DPDP Act 2023 essentials, no journalistic exemption, Sec 44(3); fake news and deepfakes — Sec 505/353 BNS, 66D, personality rights, EC advisories; platforms — Digital India Bill, competition; the online synthesis of press freedom
